items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: So I’ve been doing plenty of other gigs and still working with people like Kenny Barron and Toots

ctx.x: Okay. So you’ll be doing some commuting from coast to coast?

Yes. I have been commuting. As the old vaudeville joke goes, and my arms are tired. Back and forth. I think it’s seven times since August, back and forth, seven or eight times. So it’ll probably continue maybe five times or so during the next semester. And then of course I’m free from the middle of May until the end of August. So I’ve been doing plenty of other gigs and still working with people like Kenny Barron and Toots

Thielmans, all during this time, from being there, and have some other projects that I’m involved in. One is a French project that takes me over there a couple of times a year minimum. And I would really like to get my own show back on the road but that’s had to take a back burner by necessity because there’s so much else going on.

items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: At one time we had Ben Riley and Ray Drummond, and some other people

ctx.x: Can you talk about how you got in the band and talk a little bit more about that tenure, since that seems to have been important?

The first – I worked with him once, the first time. I don’t know where he got my number from. But I took Chick Corea’s place. It was kind of like a Return to Forever band, or whatever you want to call it. It was Tony Williams and Stanley Clarke. I guess Chick couldn’t do some gigs. So he called me. I did – it was for about a month, maybe. We did some concerts. We played down South, in Raleigh/Durham and a few other gigs, the Left Bank in Maryland. That was it. Then I didn’t hear from him for a while. Then I…

The record – the historical record’s showing that it’s from 1986 to – then People Time was 1991. Then some people say ’92. I’m not sure if the confusions for that is – because when I went to go pick it up, there were two different issues. There was one that was a single CD. Then the one that was more recently released is a double LP with – so there must – you said there were two concerts. Maybe they released the stuff . . .
